rationale:
# Rationale  
The chosen topology is an inductively-degenerated common-source LNA with a tapped capacitive load, optimized for narrowband operation at 3.5 GHz. This structure provides excellent input matching through the inductive degeneration (Lg) and resonant tuning via the tapped capacitor (Ct1/Ct2), enabling a high-Q input network that achieves S11 ≤ -14 dB while maintaining low noise figure. The inductor Lg provides series inductive feedback that enhances input impedance matching without degrading gain or noise performance. The tapped capacitor (Ct1/Ct2) forms a resonant tank with Ld, allowing high gain (S21 ≥ 17 dB) at the center frequency, and the series Ls at the source provides additional inductive degeneration for improved linearity and noise matching. The topology avoids floating nodes and uses only three inductors—within the allowed limit—and maintains a compact device count (under the device budget of 16), enabling efficient use of the 45nm CMOS process. The architecture is robust to process variations, with the input match being structurally decoupled from the output swing, thus avoiding the match-swing trade-offs described in the playbook.
